set up 
```{r}

library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(MuMIn)  # This package has functions for R-squared values for lmer models
library(performance)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

folder <- ""
setwd(folder)
nsim <- 50

setwd("your_working_directory")
getwd()


#### ----------- 1. Load data and standardize the covariates for better modeling------------ ####

#### Load and organize data
final <- read.csv("data.csv")
final$Est_log <- log(final$Est)
final[is.na(final)] <- 0
final$Year <- str_sub(final$uniqueID, -4)
final <- final %>%
  filter(Layer == "est")

#add column for name 
final$name <- sub("_.*$", "", final$uniqueID)
table(final$name)
#How many unique birds are there?
unique(final$name)

#### Standardize covariates by subtracting the mean and dividing by standard deviation
final <- final %>% mutate(
  Roads_normalized_s = (Roads_normalized - mean(Roads_normalized)) / sd(Roads_normalized),
  CC_Mean_s = (CC_mean - mean(CC_mean)) / sd(CC_mean),
  CC_stdev_s = (CC_stdev - mean(CC_stdev)) / sd(CC_stdev),
  Herb_Crop_s = (Herb_Crop - mean(Herb_Crop)) / sd(Herb_Crop),
  Nat_Herb_s = (Nat_Herb - mean(Nat_Herb)) / sd(Nat_Herb),
  Days_used_s = (Days_used - mean(Days_used)) / sd(Days_used), 
  Points_s = (Points - mean(Points)) / sd(Points)
)
```

one ecoregion at a time 
```{r}

#run model just for one eco-region
final_open <- final %>%
  filter(Ecosystem_condensed == "Open")
sum(final$Ecosystem_condensed== "Open")

#for forested
final_forested <- final %>%
  filter(Ecosystem_condensed %in% c("Mixed Forests", "Northern Boreal"))

#combine open and forested 
final_open_forested <- final %>%
  mutate(Ecoregion_grouped = case_when(
    Ecosystem_condensed %in% c("Forest", "Taiga") ~ "Forested",
    TRUE ~ Ecosystem_condensed))

#### Run the mixed effects model

#test for effects of latitude
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Longitude + (1|name), data = final)

#everything together (to test for collinearity)
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Roads_normalized_s + CC_Mean_s + CC_stdev_s + Herb_Crop_s + Nat_Herb_s + Ecosystem_condensed + (1|name), data = final)

check_collinearity(mod)

#test for forested
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Roads_normalized_s + Sex + CC_Mean_s + CC_stdev_s + Herb_Crop_s + Nat_Herb_s + (1|name), data = final_forested)

#test for sex interactions
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Nat_Herb_s*Sex + (1|name), data = final)

#test for open 
#replace variable to test individually and rerun
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Herb_Crop_s + (1|name), data = final_open)

#test for ecoregions
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Ecosystem_condensed + Sex + (1|name), data = final)

emmeans(mod, pairwise ~ Ecosystem_condensed)

#test for total points and days used
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Points_s + Days_used_s + (1|name), data = final)
#check cor
cor(final$Points, final$Days_used, use = "complete.obs")

#plot total days used
ggplot(final, aes(x = Days_used, y = Est_log)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

#plot total points
ggplot(final, aes(x = Points, y = Est_log)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

## R-squared value to assess how well the model fits
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(object = mod)
qqnorm(resid(mod))
check_collinearity(mod)

#### ---------------------------------- 3. CIs -------------------------------------- ####

#### Generate CIs with bootMer
simsCI <- bootMer(mod, FUN=fixef, nsim=500) # "fixef" means bootstrapping fixed effects estimates
dim(simsCI$t) # the "t" object has 500 estimates for each of our fixed effects!
# View(simsCI$t)
apply(simsCI$t, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))  # 95% CIs on the coefficients 

## Organize CIs to export for manuscript table
CIs <- apply(simsCI$t, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))  
estimates <- data.frame(Covariate = colnames(simsCI$t),
                        Mean = round(fixef(mod), 2),
                        Lower95 = round(CIs[1, ], 2),
                        Upper95 = round(CIs[2, ], 2))

estimates

```

plotting effects for forested and open
```{r}
#for all forested only (mixed forests plus northern boreal)

# Data
effects <- data.frame(
  Covariate = c("Intercept",
                "Sex (M)",
                "Roads",
                "Canopy Cover Mean",
                "Canopy Cover SD",
                "Herbaceous Croplands",
                "Natural Herbaceous"),
  Mean = c(0.3, 1.92, -0.38, 0.07, 0.34, -0.39, 0.1),
  Lower95 = c(-0.1, 1.39, -0.62, -0.31, 0.01, -0.86, -0.31),
  Upper95 = c(0.71, 2.39, -0.16, 0.38, 0.71, 0.09, 0.52)
)

# Order from top to bottom
effects$Covariate <- factor(
  effects$Covariate,
  levels = rev(effects$Covariate)
)

pdf(file="Forested_all_variables.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

forest_plot <- ggplot(effects, aes(x = Mean, y = Covariate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Lower95, xmax = Upper95),
                 height = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Effects for Forested Ecoregions",
    x = "Effect estimate (95% CI)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )

ggsave("forest_effects.pdf", plot = forest_plot,
       width = 7, height = 5, units = "in")

```

plotting-- for all variables (original)
```{r}

#need this for Forested: roads, canopy cover SD and for open herbaceous croplands + sex nat herb forested

#start with forested 

#### ----------------------- 4. Generate predictions for plotting --------------------------------- ####

nsim <- 50

#### Generate predictions for plotting
# In order to make a pretty plot, we need to give the model a series of x values 
# and have it predict y values. Just like with fixed effects estimates above, 
# it's easy to get mean predictions but more complicated to get uncertainty. 
# We'll need to use the bootMer function again to get CIs on the predictions. 

## Start by making a sequence for the covariates we want to plot
x.CC_stdev <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_stdev_s), to = quantile(final_forested$CC_stdev_s, probs = 0.95), length.out = nsim)

x.herb_crop <- seq(from = min(final_open$Herb_Crop_s), to = max(final_open$Herb_Crop_s), length.out = nsim)
x.nat_herb <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Nat_Herb_s), to = max(final_forested$Nat_Herb_s), length.out = nsim)
x.CC_mean <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_Mean_s), to = max(final_forested$CC_Mean_s), length.out = nsim)

x.Roads_normalized_s <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s), to = max(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s), length.out = nsim)


## Generate datasets for prediction
# In order to make predictions for 1 variable, we will hold all other variables at their means
# Because we standardized covariates, the means are all 0 (or very close to 0)
new.data.CC_stdev <- data.frame(Sex = "M",    
                                Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                CC_Mean_s = 0,
                                CC_stdev_s = x.CC_stdev,
                                Herb_Crop_s = 0,
                                Nat_Herb_s = 0)
new.data.herb_crop <- data.frame(Sex = "M",    
                                Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                CC_Mean_s = 0,
                                CC_stdev_s = 0,
                                Herb_Crop_s = x.herb_crop,
                                Nat_Herb_s = 0)
new.data.nat_herb <- data.frame(Sex = "M",    
                                Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                CC_Mean_s = 0,
                                CC_stdev_s = 0,
                                Herb_Crop_s = 0,
                                Nat_Herb_s = x.nat_herb)

new.data.CC_mean <- data.frame(Sex = "M",    
                                Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                CC_Mean_s = x.CC_mean,
                                CC_stdev_s = 0,
                                Herb_Crop_s = 0,
                                Nat_Herb_s = 0)

new.data.Roads_normalized <- data.frame(Sex = "M",    
                                Roads_normalized_s = x.Roads_normalized_s,
                                CC_Mean_s = 0,
                                CC_stdev_s = 0,
                                Herb_Crop_s = 0,
                                Nat_Herb_s = 0)

## Generate predictions of the mean relationship
?predict.merMod # information on what the predict function is doing here. 

pred.CC_stdev <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form=NA, 
                        newdata = new.data.CC_stdev)
pred.herb_crop <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form=NA, 
                         newdata = new.data.herb_crop)
pred.nat_herb <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form=NA, 
                          newdata = new.data.nat_herb)
pred.CC_mean <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form=NA, 
                         newdata = new.data.CC_mean)
pred.Roads_normalized <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form=NA, 
                         newdata = new.data.Roads_normalized)


## Generate confidence intervals on predictions for CC_stdev, Herb_Crop, and Nat_Herb
CI.CC_stdev <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim, 
                       FUN=function(x) {predict(x, newdata = new.data.CC_stdev, type = "response", re.form = NA) }) 
CI.herb_crop <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim, 
                       FUN=function(x) {predict(x, newdata = new.data.herb_crop, type = "response", re.form = NA) }) 

CI.nat_herb <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim, 
                       FUN=function(x) {predict(x, newdata = new.data.nat_herb, type = "response", re.form = NA) }) 

CI.CC_mean <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim, 
                       FUN=function(x) {predict(x, newdata = new.data.CC_mean, type = "response", re.form = NA) }) 

CI.Roads_normalized <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim, 
                       FUN=function(x) {predict(x, newdata = new.data.Roads_normalized, type = "response", re.form = NA) }) 

#### ------------------------- 5. Finally, we're ready to plot! ---------------------------- ####
# I'm using base R code similar to Courtney's class here, but you should feel free to use ggplot

## Create sequences of covariates NOT on the standardized scale
x.CC_stdev.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_stdev), to = quantile(final_forested$CC_stdev, probs = 0.95), length.out = nsim)
x.herb_crop.raw <- seq(from = min(final_open$Herb_Crop), to = max(final_open$Herb_Crop), length.out = nsim)
x.nat_herb.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Nat_Herb), to = max(final_forested$Nat_Herb), length.out = nsim)
x.CC_mean.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_Mean), to = max(final_forested$CC_Mean), length.out = nsim)

x.Roads_normalized.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s), to = max(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s), length.out = nsim)


#### 3-panel plot with Herb_Crop on top, y axis on the data scale

```
Plotting
```{r}

pdf(file="Forested_all_variables.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

par(mfrow = c(2,2), mar = c(3,3,1,1), tcl = 0.3, mgp = c(1.5,0.2,0), las= 1,
    cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.8)

## Herbaceous Croplands
plot(x = x.herb_crop.raw, y = pred.herb_crop, ylim = c(0,3.3), bty="l", type="n",
     xlab = "% cover herbaceous croplands" , ylab="log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.herb_crop.raw, rev(x.herb_crop.raw)), 
        c(apply(CI.herb_crop$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T), 
          rev(apply(CI.herb_crop$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T))), col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.herb_crop.raw, y = pred.herb_crop, col = "black", lwd = 2)

## Natural Herbaceous
plot.new()  # skips the top right panel
plot(x = x.nat_herb.raw, y = pred.nat_herb, ylim = c(0,3.3), bty="l", type="n",
     xlab = "% cover natural herbaceous" , ylab="log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.nat_herb.raw, rev(x.nat_herb.raw)), 
        c(apply(CI.nat_herb$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T), 
          rev(apply(CI.nat_herb$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T))), col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.nat_herb.raw, y = pred.nat_herb, col = "black", lwd = 2)

## Standard deviation of CC
plot(x = x.CC_stdev.raw, y = pred.CC_stdev, ylim = c(0,3.3), bty="l", type="n",
     xlab = "Standard deviation of canopy cover" , ylab="log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.CC_stdev.raw, rev(x.CC_stdev.raw)), 
        c(apply(CI.CC_stdev$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T), 
          rev(apply(CI.CC_stdev$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T))), col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.CC_stdev.raw, y = pred.CC_stdev, col = "black", lwd = 2)


dev.off()

plot(x = x.CC_mean.raw, y = pred.CC_mean, ylim = c(0,3.3), bty="l", type="n",
     xlab = "Canopy cover Mean" , ylab="log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.CC_mean.raw, rev(x.CC_mean.raw)), 
        c(apply(CI.CC_mean$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T), 
          rev(apply(CI.CC_mean$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T))), col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.CC_mean.raw, y = pred.CC_mean, col = "black", lwd = 2)
```
